engine_name: ExLlamaV2 / ExLlamaV3 (turboderp-org) served via tabbyAPI (theroyallab). ExLlamaV2 latest = v0.3.2 (Jul 2025, EXL2 format). ExLlamaV3 latest = v0.0.43 (Jun 14 2026, EXL3/QTIP format). Gemma 4 support lives in ExLlamaV3, NOT ExLlamaV2. tabbyAPI is the official OpenAI-compatible API server for both backends.
cuda_128_compatible: Yes for ExLlamaV3 (the relevant engine for Gemma 4). ExLlamaV3 v0.0.43 ships prebuilt cu128 wheels on the GitHub releases page, built against torch 2.10.0 for cp310-cp314 on linux_x86_64 (e.g. exllamav3-0.0.43+cu128.torch2.10.0-cp313-cp313-linux_x86_64.whl, ~185 MB). This matches NVIDIA driver 570.195 / CUDA 12.8 max / sm_86 (A6000 is sm_86, well within Ampere support). Critical caveat: the wheel ABI is pinned to a specific torch build, so you MUST install the exact torch version the wheel was built against (torch 2.10.0 + cu128) or the C++ extension will fail to load. ExLlamaV2 also publishes cu12x wheels historically but its Gemma 4 status is the blocker, not CUDA. PyPI `pip install exllamav3` is available but compiles from source locally (needs CUDA toolkit + nvcc, a multi-minute to multi-hour build). Recommended path: install the matching prebuilt cu128 wheel directly from the GitHub release URL to avoid source compilation. [uncertain: whether the exact cp version you need is in the 52-asset list; verify on the releases page]
gemma4_support: Gemma 4 31B dense IS supported, but ONLY via ExLlamaV3 (EXL3 format), not ExLlamaV2 (EXL2 format). ExLlamaV3 v0.0.40 added `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` / `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`. Official quants exist on HuggingFace: `turboderp/gemma-4-31b-it-exl3` (dense 31B) and `turboderp/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-exl3` (MoE), with multiple bpw branches (e.g. 4.10bpw, 6.0bpw). Format required is EXL3 (a streamlined QTIP variant), NOT the older EXL2 used by ExLlamaV2. Known architectural gaps in ExLlamaV3: no tensor/expert parallelism for Gemma 4, and the E2B/E4B variants are unsupported (only 31B dense and 26B MoE work). The 31B dense model is reported to be sensitive to quantization errors and can produce gibberish if config is imperfect. ExLlamaV2 (EXL2) only ever documented up to Gemma 3 (v0.2.9); no Gemma 4 EXL2 quants surfaced, so the 'ExLlamaV2' part of this research item is effectively superseded by ExLlamaV3 for Gemma 4.
per_request_reasoning_toggle: Partially. tabbyAPI exposes a global `reasoning` parser config plus `force_enable_thinking` (injects `enable_thinking: True` into the chat template args; intended as a server-side default because some clients/models need it to enter reasoning mode). For per-request control, tabbyAPI supports HF Jinja2 chat templates and passes generation parameters through, so `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` in the request body is the canonical Gemma 4 mechanism to disable thinking on a per-request basis (this is the documented Gemma 4 pattern across the ecosystem and works where the template honors it). The exact field is `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`. Whether tabbyAPI plumbs `chat_template_kwargs` through reliably for every request was not explicitly confirmed in the wiki (it points to the autogenerated /docs OpenAPI for the full param list). [uncertain: confirmation that tabbyAPI forwards per-request chat_template_kwargs to the Gemma 4 template without being overridden by force_enable_thinking]
per_request_reasoning_budget: No clear native per-request reasoning/thinking-token budget was found for tabbyAPI as of mid-2026. Unlike NVIDIA NIM (`reasoning_budget`), vLLM (`thinking_token_budget` / chat_template_kwargs), llama.cpp (`reasoning_budget`), or Anthropic (`thinking.budget_tokens`), the tabbyAPI wiki and config_sample expose a reasoning *parser* and `force_enable_thinking` but no documented logits-processor that force-injects `</think>` after N tokens. You can disable thinking entirely (budget=0 equivalent via enable_thinking:false) and you can cap total output with `max_tokens`, but capping ONLY the reasoning segment per request is not a documented first-class feature. This is the same gap the research brief flags for llama.cpp. Verify against the live OpenAPI docs (http://localhost:5000/docs) of a running instance. [uncertain: existence of an undocumented or recently-added reasoning-budget sampler in tabbyAPI/ExLlamaV3]
tool_calling_support: tabbyAPI explicitly lists `gemma4` as a supported `tool_format` value (in the Tool Calling wiki, alongside qwen3_coder, glm4_5, minimax_m2, mistral). The implementation aligns with the OpenAI Tools standard (no modified Jinja templates required in the revamped system): you pass OpenAI-style `tools` and `tool_choice`, and tabbyAPI parses model output into structured `tool_calls`. To use it you must (a) load a prompt_template that supports tool calling and (b) set `tool_format: gemma4`; if `tool_format` is blank the server will NOT parse tool calls. Reliability caveat: tool calling for Gemma 4 depends on reasoning being enabled — some clients (e.g. OpenCode) do not enable reasoning by default, which degrades Gemma 4 tool calling; the documented workaround is `force_enable_thinking: true`. General ecosystem caveat from the maintainers: the tool-calling standard is evolving and 'no two clients agree' on the exact shape, so streaming partial tool calls / multi-turn behavior should be tested. No Gemma4-specific tool-call truncation bug surfaced, but reliability at scale is not independently benchmarked. [uncertain: real-world reliability of gemma4 tool_format under streaming and multi-turn]
openai_api_compatible: Yes. tabbyAPI is a FastAPI server exposing an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions (and /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings) endpoint with SSE streaming, aligned to the OpenAI spec including OpenAI-style tools/tool_calls. It adds extended (non-OpenAI) generation parameters (e.g. min_p, repetition_penalty, sampler overrides) which are optional and won't break a standard openai-python / httpx asyncio client. One known OpenAI-compat wrinkle generic to Gemma 4 thinking models: if thinking is enabled and not handled, responses can return only a reasoning field with empty content; mitigated by enable_thinking:false or proper reasoning-parser config so `content` is populated.
continuous_batching: Yes (ExLlamaV3). ExLlamaV3's feature list explicitly includes 'continuous, dynamic batching', so concurrent requests are not serialized. For the target workload (1 dev + up to 10 concurrent users / 4-8 parallel sub-agents) this is adequate and is a real advantage over a naive sequential setup. ExLlamaV2 also has a dynamic generator with batching. Continuous batching is beneficial here but not strictly mandatory at this small scale; it does help avoid head-of-line blocking when sub-agents fire in parallel.
installation_steps:
Host-native (no Docker), Ubuntu/Debian RunPod pod, CUDA 12.8, Python 3.12 example:

# 1. Create venv
python3.12 -m venv ~/tabby-venv && source ~/tabby-venv/bin/activate

# 2. Install torch matching the ExLlamaV3 wheel ABI (cu128, torch 2.10.0)
pip install torch==2.10.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

# 3. Install the prebuilt ExLlamaV3 cu128 wheel (pick cp matching your Python)
pip install https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/releases/download/v0.0.43/exllamav3-0.0.43+cu128.torch2.10.0-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl

# 4. Clone and install tabbyAPI (official server for ExLlama)
git clone https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI && cd tabbyAPI
pip install -e .
# (tabbyAPI also has a start script that can auto-select the matching exllama wheel)

# 5. Download the Gemma 4 EXL3 quant (e.g. 4.x bpw branch to fit 48GB)
# via tabbyAPI's built-in HF downloader or huggingface-cli, model: turboderp/gemma-4-31b-it-exl3

Notes: avoid `pip install exllamav3` from PyPI unless you want a source build (needs nvcc/CUDA toolkit). The exact wheel filename (cp version, torch version) must match your environment exactly. [uncertain: exact wheel URL/filename — verify the asset list on the v0.0.43 release page]
serve_command:
Using tabbyAPI with a config.yml (tabbyAPI is config-file driven rather than long CLI flags):

# config.yml (excerpt)
network:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8000
model:
  model_dir: /path/to/models
  model_name: gemma-4-31b-it-exl3   # the downloaded EXL3 quant dir
  max_seq_len: 16384
  cache_mode: Q4                    # or Q6/Q8; Q4 KV-cache to save VRAM
  prompt_template: gemma4          # tool-calling-capable template
  tool_format: gemma4              # enables OpenAI-style tool parsing
  reasoning: true                  # enable reasoning parser
  reasoning_start_token: "<think>"
  reasoning_end_token: "</think>"
  # force_enable_thinking: true    # optional, if clients omit enable_thinking

Then launch:
  python main.py --config config.yml

Per-request: disable thinking with body `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}`; pass OpenAI `tools` for tool calling. [uncertain: exact config keys reasoning_end_token vs reasoning_stop_token and whether cache_mode Q4 is the literal value — confirm against config_sample.yml]
speculative_decoding: Yes. ExLlamaV3's feature list explicitly includes speculative decoding (draft model), and tabbyAPI exposes draft-model config (draft model dir + draft cache settings). However, the Gemma 4 MTP draft asset referenced in the brief (mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf, GGUF/MTP) is a llama.cpp-format MTP head and is NOT directly usable by ExLlamaV3, which needs an EXL3-format draft model sharing the Gemma 4 vocabulary. A small Gemma 4 EXL3 model (e.g. E2B/E4B) would be the natural draft, but ExLlamaV3 currently lists E2B/E4B as unsupported, which undercuts the easiest speculative-decoding path for Gemma 4 specifically. Expected single-stream speedup from speculative decoding is typically ~1.5-2x when a good draft exists; at small concurrent load the benefit shrinks as batching fills the GPU. [uncertain: whether any compatible EXL3 Gemma 4 draft model exists; MTP-style draft support in ExLlamaV3 for Gemma 4]
known_issues_gemma4: 1) High VRAM bug: ExLlamaV3 GitHub issue #191 (open, unresolved) reports gemma-4-31B-it-exl3 at 6.0bpw consuming ~85.3 GiB at 131k context vs ~46.8 GiB for the 26B MoE at 262k context and ~45.2 GiB for the same 31B under llama.cpp Q6_K at 262k — roughly 4x more VRAM than expected for the dense model. This strongly affects A6000 48GB: 6.0bpw at long context will NOT fit; you must drop to ~4.0bpw and/or 16k context. 2) No tensor/expert parallelism for Gemma 4 in ExLlamaV3. 3) E2B/E4B variants unsupported. 4) 31B dense is quant-sensitive and can emit gibberish if config is wrong. 5) Gemma 4 thinking-mode empty-content pitfall (content empty when only reasoning is returned) — generic across engines, mitigated via reasoning parser / enable_thinking:false. 6) tool calling reliability tied to reasoning being enabled (OpenCode default disables it). Sources: exllamav3 issues #191, tabbyAPI Tool Calling wiki.
vram_usage: At 4-bit-equivalent EXL3 (~4.0-4.25 bpw) with 16k context, the 31B dense weights are roughly ~16-18 GB plus KV cache. With Q4 KV cache at 16k, total is plausibly ~22-28 GB, leaving comfortable headroom on A6000 48GB for the bge-small-en-v1.5 embedder (0.13 GB) and bge-reranker-v2-m3 (2.3 GB) co-resident. HOWEVER, the open VRAM-overhead bug (#191) shows the dense 31B can use far more than the math predicts (~4x at higher bpw/context), so DO NOT plan for 6.0bpw or long context on 48GB — stick to ~4.0bpw and 16k, and measure actual usage before adding co-resident models. By comparison llama.cpp Q6_K fits the same model at much longer context in ~45 GiB, so llama.cpp is currently more VRAM-efficient for Gemma 4 31B. [uncertain: exact EXL3 4.0bpw + 16k VRAM figure given the unresolved overhead bug]
small_scale_fit: Marginal-to-poor right now for this specific model. The engine family (ExLlamaV3 + tabbyAPI) is well-suited to single-GPU small deployments in general (lightweight, fast EXL3 quants, continuous batching, OpenAI API), and tabbyAPI is genuinely simple to operate. BUT for Gemma 4 31B dense the combination of (a) the unresolved 4x VRAM-overhead bug, (b) no per-request reasoning budget, (c) speculative-decoding draft gap, and (d) wheel/torch-ABI pinning fragility means the operational overhead does NOT clearly beat the simpler llama.cpp baseline at this scale. ExLlamaV3 is still maturing (README warns 'some things may be a little broken at first'). For a single dev + <=10 users, llama.cpp's better Gemma 4 VRAM efficiency and broader, more stable Gemma 4 support make it the safer default until issue #191 is fixed.
overall_recommendation: VIABLE (with caveats), leaning NOT_VIABLE for the dense 31B specifically until the VRAM bug is fixed. PROS: prebuilt cu128 wheels for ExLlamaV3 (works on A6000/CUDA 12.8), official Gemma 4 31B EXL3 quants on HF, tabbyAPI exposes a dedicated `gemma4` tool_format (a real advantage — first-class tool parsing), clean OpenAI-compatible streaming API, continuous batching, host-native install (no Docker), very fast EXL3 kernels and excellent quant quality. CONS: Gemma 4 support is in ExLlamaV3 (EXL3), not ExLlamaV2 (EXL2) as the item title implies; open ExLlamaV3 issue #191 shows ~4x VRAM overhead for the 31B dense model, which risks not fitting A6000 48GB at useful context/bpw; no documented per-request reasoning *budget* (only on/off via enable_thinking) — the core requirement the brief cares about is unmet just like llama.cpp; speculative-decoding draft path for Gemma 4 is unclear (MTP GGUF draft is not EXL3-compatible, E2B/E4B unsupported); wheel/torch ABI must be matched exactly; engine still maturing. RECOMMENDATION: keep llama.cpp as baseline; treat ExLlamaV3+tabbyAPI as a strong candidate to revisit once #191 (VRAM) is resolved and reasoning-budget support lands — its gemma4 tool_format is the single most compelling reason to consider it.
